speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) for each year from 2021 to 2023, what is the number of vaping feedback received by the Health Science Authority (HSA) from the public, educational institutions, Police and the Central Narcotics Bureau, respectively; (b) what is the size of HSA’s enforcement team dedicated to vaping enforcement; (c) what is the number of summons on vaping offences issued by HSA in the last three years; and (d) how many summons are issued in collaboration with other law enforcement agencies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We do not have readily available data on the breakdown of the feedback sources.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Cases which require a Notice of Composition to be issued are handled by HSA.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: I just want to ask a couple of supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: The first is: has the size of HSA's enforcement team grown for the past three years, since I see that the figures for violations for vaping have increased quite steadily?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Two, is the agency also getting help from the Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) and the Police Force to help in the enforcement.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Three, we read about the multi-agency approach to vaping enforcement as well as the importing of vaping equipment.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Can Ms Rahayu give more details on how this is set up and what are the key performance indicators (KPIs) to be met?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We note the concern and the approach that we are taking is, as mentioned, that we are looking at a multi-agency approach.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We do have to look at this issue from a multi-pronged perspective as well.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are taking the approach of outsourcing some of the enforcement measures.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The agencies will cross enforce, meaning that if there are agencies that take up and pick up some of these cases of vaping, it is referred to HSA and HSA can then issue the necessary Notice of Composition.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The Member had also asked whether the Police is also involved in this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: If they go out and as they do their own work, and they do discover cases of vaping, they will refer these cases to HSA, and also at many different fronts, because this issue, as you know, is a big one.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: At the front where it relates to the sale and the advertisement of the products online, we are working with the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) and the Infocomm Media Development Authority.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is where we are working with other agencies to track and stop the efforts of people selling all these products online.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are working with the agencies in the community, as I mentioned earlier, with NEA, NParks, the Police, in the community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: When they catch these cases, these cases are referred to us and then we issue the Notice of Composition or do the necessary enforcement.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The schools work with us to look at education and informing the public about it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These are some of the various efforts of how this multi-agency collaboration effort works.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And if there is a need, we can definitely size the manpower and adjust our manpower accordingly to address the problem.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: At this juncture, because it is something that happens in multi-facets of people's lives – I mean, we also have to consider things like at the borders when things get smuggled in – so, we do need to take that approach of working together with all these other agencies collectively, so that we can have a more effective response to the growing problem.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: But at this point in time, when a member of the public or the schools call the Police for help in vaping enforcement, they will be asked to refer it to HSA.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: So, I hope HSA can work with the different agencies to have a no-wrong-door policy to deal with this feedback, rather than all go to HSA, which is a very modest set-up, as you said.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: We do not want to have a young generation that is a vaping generation in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: If he has some specific issues that have arisen, please do let us know.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is something that we have also progressed over time.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Initially, perhaps, there may have been some apprehension with regard to the other agencies getting involved in this, but we had recently announced the multi-agency effort, so, I think there is better coordination now between the agencies.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are looking at how we can make sure that the different aspects are dealt with.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: For example, if it is a complaint to schools, the schools will look at it with disciplinary proceedings as well.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: At the same time now, we are also making sure that HSA is kept apprised of this and the necessary compositions are issued.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But I note your concerns about the enforcement measures all being handled by HSA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, at this juncture, the enforcement bit of that, in terms of issuing of composition as well as any action taken in Court, is done by HSA.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But actually, there are other aspects of the work – there is the catching, there is education, there is also checking at the borders, there is checking on the online space – which all need collective effort from different agencies.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: One, will more agencies come on board as part of this cross-enforcement project?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And two, will HSA continue to take the lead on this issue and ensure that, amongst the agencies involved, processes will be aligned, protocols will be made smoother in the apprehension of people who have vaporisers?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will continue to assess and monitor the situation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: When we are involving all these agencies, there is some thought to it.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: These are the agencies that are relevant in the problem.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: They are involved because, as I mentioned earlier, there are different aspects of the issue which we want to resolve, and their support and action is also necessary.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We need to figure out what is the best approach.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It is not just about bringing all different agencies in, but how can they meaningfully come on board to work together.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are looking at how we can ensure effective enforcement and deploy resources meaningfully.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I guess that addresses his first question about whether there are other agencies coming on board.
